note: Cases built from fixtures run through `orb validate --json` (the Rust check): the OAuth client shapes (tag, mode, clientAuth, clientId, issuer or endpoints, endpoints and their keys, a client that is not an object) on `oauth-authorize`, which carried the same client check as the retired `http` oauth-client auth (the cases keep their findings and messages and name the effect that now holds the client); oauth-authorize, oauth-connection-status and oauth-connection-forget; literal issuer and endpoint URLs against `egress` (default ports, case, schemes, clients keyed by provider), the default port of each scheme coming from `browser/beacon` in the operator table; and the emit block of the three effects. The `http` cases (op words, endpoint mismatch, request conflict, `clients` map, provider key) were retired with the `http` operator (EXEC-HTTP-1). The collector answer is the HOST_CALLS_COLLECTED the shared collector gives for the same program; the emit-config answer holds the findings Rust reports for each emit object.
